policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders only the two προλέγω verbs ("I have said beforehand, and I do say beforehand") and carries the sentence through to "I will not spare"; there is no rendering of an added γράφω ("I write") after "so now, being absent". The notes are alternative_rendering and do not bear on the unit.

ASV reads "for he was crucified through weakness" as a flat causal statement, not the conditional "for if he was crucified" that εἰ γὰρ requires; no "if" is rendered or supplied. The textual_variant note concerns "with" for the following prepositional phrase, not this unit.

ζήσομεν and ζησόμεθα are active and middle futures of the same verb in the same person and number; both come into English as "we shall live", so the ASV wording cannot distinguish them. The mapped textual_variant note ("Many ancient authorities read with") addresses the phrase rendered "toward you" and names no reading in this set.
ASV reads "that Jesus Christ is in you", the order of Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς; the transposed Χριστὸς Ἰησοῦς is rendered "Christ Jesus" throughout the ASV, so the printed name order distinguishes the reading.

English requires a copula in "Jesus Christ is in you" whether or not ἐστίν stands in the Greek, and the ASV does not italicize "is" here as a supply; the wording therefore settles nothing between the two readings.
ASV reads "Now we pray to God", first person plural, matching εὐχόμεθα; the singular Εὐχόμαι would be "I pray". The greek_gloss note concerns the following conjunction, not the verb.

ASV renders καί as "also" but sets the clause off with a colon ("and ye are strong: this we also pray for"), and it leaves a connective δέ unrendered where the punctuation already carries the break; the absence of "but" or "and" therefore does not exclude the added δὲ. No note is mapped here.

The variant is word order alone within the relative clause, and English syntax fixes "which the Lord gave me" regardless of whether ὁ κύριος stands before or after ἔδωκέν μοι; the ASV cannot show the Greek order here.
The ASV verse ends at "All the saints salute you." with no "Amen", which the ASV renders wherever it accepts a closing Ἀμήν; the added word is absent from the English.
